The '''2002 Ohio gubernatorial election''' took place on November 5, 2002. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Governor of Ohio]] [[Bob Taft]] ran for a second and final term as governor. He was opposed by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee [[Tim Hagan]], a former [[Cuyahoga County, Ohio|Cuyahoga County]] commissioner. The race between Taft and Hagan was not competitive; Taft was re-elected by a substantial margin.

As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, this was the last time that someone other than a current or former member of Congress was elected to the governorship.

==Democratic primary==

===Candidates===
*[[Tim Hagan]], former [[Cuyahoga County, Ohio|Cuyahoga County]] commissioner and candidate for Cleveland mayor in [[1989 Cleveland mayoral election#Primary election|1989]]

=== Declined ===

* [[Sherrod Brown]], U.S. representative from [[Ohio's 13th congressional district]] since 1993, [[Ohio secretary of state]] 1983-1991<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Wenzel |first=Fritz |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Rw4wAAAAIBAJ&dq=sherrod+brown+redistricting+2002&pg=PA4&article_id=6645,4983086 |title=A predictable political year ahead |publisher=Toledo Blade |date=2001-12-31 |pages=7A |language=en}}</ref>
* [[Dick Celeste|Richard Celeste]], [[List of ambassadors of the United States to India|U.S. ambassador to India]] 1997–2001, former governor of Ohio 1983-1991<ref>{{Cite book |last=Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9adQAAAAIBAJ&dq=sherrod+brown+governor+2002&pg=PA6&article_id=2673,1521975 |title=Hagan may run for governor |publisher=Portsmouth Daily Times |date=2001-05-09 |pages=A11 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=P8hIAAAAIBAJ&dq=celeste+ohio+governor+2001&pg=PA7&article_id=4277,6461814 |title=Politics are not in Celeste's plans |publisher=The Vindicator |date=2001-04-28 |pages=B4 |language=en}}</ref>

Sherrod Brown's district was seen as particularly vulnerable in redistricting, and many thought he would run for governor.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Skolnick |first=David |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3o1cAAAAIBAJ&dq=sherrod+brown+redistricting&pg=PA8&article_id=1049,4052614 |title=Brown hints at run for governor's job |publisher=The Vindicator |date=2001-04-04 |pages=B4 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Wenzel |first=Fritz |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=n4UUAAAAIBAJ&dq=sherrod+brown+redistricting&pg=PA3&article_id=6928,248295 |title=GOP holds edge in redrawing Ohio political map |publisher=Toledo Blade |date=2001-03-17 |pages=A4 |language=en}}</ref> Brown ultimately did not pursue a race, and went on to win in a redrawn 13th district.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CNN.com Election 2002 - State Races: Ohio |url=http://www.cnn.com/ELECTION/2002/pages/states/OH/index.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030212062924/http://www.cnn.com/ELECTION/2002/pages/states/OH/index.html |archive-date=2003-02-12 |access-date=2023-08-26 |website=www.cnn.com}}</ref> Tim Hagan, a former Cuyahoga County commissioner, had initially dithered on running, indicating a willingness to defer to a more prominent nominee, should one emerge.<ref>{{Cite book |last=McCarthy |first=John |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OtIJAAAAIBAJ&dq=tim+hagan+2002&pg=PA8&article_id=4271,3820027 |title=Partisans have no choice at the top - again |publisher=The Bryan Times |date=2002-05-02 |pages=8 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> As none emerged, Hagan became the Democratic nominee.

==General election==
Taft was the favorite, and Hagan struggled with fundraising.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Drew |first=James |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pQ0wAAAAIBAJ&dq=tim+hagan+2002&pg=PA3&article_id=5312,4531729 |title=Hagan falls behind Taft in quest for campaign cash |publisher=Toledo Blade |date=2002-06-15 |pages=A4 |language=en}}</ref> Hagan, who was married to ''Star Trek'' actress [[Kate Mulgrew]], held a fundraiser with her and [[William Shatner]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VexIAAAAIBAJ&dq=tim+hagan+2002&pg=PA22&article_id=3193,5389640 |title='Star Trek' Fans raise $150,000 for Tim Hagan |publisher=The Vindicator |date=2002-08-25 |pages=B5 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2002-08-27 |title=CNN.com - Let the debates begin - August 27, 2002 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2002/ALLPOLITICS/08/24/week.ahead/index.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20021004123556/https://www.cnn.com/2002/ALLPOLITICS/08/24/week.ahead/index.html |archive-date=2002-10-04 |access-date=2023-09-02 |website=www.cnn.com}}</ref> Hagan still struggled, and had to pull TV ads and focus on mail ads.<ref>{{Cite book |last=The Vindicator Wire Report |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=U-xIAAAAIBAJ&dq=tim+hagan+2002&pg=PA18&article_id=2752,3895526 |title=Hagan forgoes TV ads, citing lack of campaign funds |publisher=The Vindicator |date=2002-08-22 |pages=B4 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iedDAAAAIBAJ&dq=tim+hagan+2002&pg=PA24&article_id=1412,3076401 |title=Hagan abandons TV for mailboxes |publisher=The Daily Sentinel |date=2002-08-23 |pages=A2 |language=en}}</ref>

===Results===
Taft won reelection easily, winning by nearly 19.5% and by 628,083 votes. He did well in most parts of the state. Hagan only managed to win six out of 88 counties. He won [[Lorain County]], [[Cuyahoga County]], [[Summit County, Ohio|Summit County]], [[Trumbull County]], [[Mahoning County]], and [[Athens County]]. Despite winning in a landslide,

Taft would go on to be extremely unpopular in his second term, leaving office with a 2% approval rating, the lowest for any statewide official in modern U.S. history.

In 2006, Democrat [[Ted Strickland]] would easily defeat Republican [[Ohio Secretary of State]] [[Ken Blackwell]]. This resulted in a gain for the Democrats, and was the first time they had obtained the governorship in 16 years.
